scores.evidence: No agenda, no recap of the requirements list Priya had already shared, generic demo data instead of a K&S-style P&L.
The real driver (GL Wand not supported on Fusion, Spreadsheet Server in the frame) came out at 41:45, and only because Vikash volunteered it.
Two IT and reporting leads attended. The demo was pitched at finance users, and architecture questions were answered verbally with no diagram.
Two live failures (cost-centre lookup at 15:00, bursting at 25:49) and a deliberately duplicated row that triggered a warning.
Security, deployment and schema answers were clear. EPM, non-finance data and implementation effort were muddled or not answered.
'Built for the enterprise' and performance were claimed without proof. GLSense and Spreadsheet Server were never addressed.
Daniel rescued the EPM and differentiation answers, but the two sellers contradicted each other on EPM availability and non-finance data.
Won the P&L template and a clear timeline (January execution, June pilot, October go-live). No date booked and the pre-brief was declined.
Drill from P&L to the Fusion invoice in a few clicks, security inheritance, formula consistency warning and fast refresh landed well.

questions.question: Do users inherit their existing Fusion access?
questions.note: Roles are pulled through, so users see the same data as in Fusion.

questions.question: Can a row combine account and cost centre?
questions.note: Cost-centre list of values errored. Logged as a follow-up action.

questions.question: Can we show actuals against budgets held in EPM (EPBCS)?
questions.note: Marc said an EPM version is 'coming'. Daniel then said it is 'available now'.

questions.question: How does drill-back from the warehouse link into Fusion?
questions.note: IDs are passed to a hidden URL in the template. Not configurable by end users.

questions.question: Does the warehouse sit inside our environment?
questions.note: On-premise, customer OCI or SplashBI-hosted OCI.

questions.question: Can it deploy as a separate schema in our existing ADW?
questions.note: Yes, separate schema or separate database.

questions.question: Do you have AI or chatbot capabilities?
questions.note: Coming 'before January', no firm date, nothing to show.

questions.question: Why choose GL Connect over GL Wand?
questions.note: Generic scale and performance claims. No proof, no named comparison.

questions.question: Is it one product for EBS history and Fusion data?
questions.note: Yes, but the warehouse versus direct connection point was confused.

questions.question: Can we combine non-finance data such as sales and work orders?
questions.note: Daniel said yes. Marc said not in GL Connect, only in the wider SplashBI product.

questions.question: How easily can we build and maintain a combined EPM and Fusion model?
questions.note: Turned into a request for K&S requirements instead.

moments.title: Invites interruptions
moments.detail: Set a conversational tone and framed GL Connect as keeping users in familiar Excel.

moments.title: Drill from P&L to Fusion source
moments.detail: Balance, journal, subledger and the Fusion invoice in a few clicks. The strongest moment of the call.

moments.title: Clear security answer
moments.detail: Fusion roles are inherited, so no second security model to maintain.

moments.title: Mistake turned into a feature
moments.detail: The formula consistency warning showed the tool catching a duplicated row.

moments.title: Concrete performance figure
moments.detail: About 900 cells refreshed in about 24 seconds on a laptop.

moments.title: Continuation sheets
moments.detail: Automatic overflow when Excel's row limit is reached, a real pain for less technical users.

moments.title: EPM cube flattening
moments.detail: Daniel positioned direct EPM reporting as something most tools cannot do.

moments.title: Flexible deployment
moments.detail: On-premise, customer OCI, SplashBI OCI, or a separate schema in their ADW.

moments.title: Found the EBS history gap
moments.detail: Daniel's question exposed that history stays in EBS, opening the EBS plus Fusion story.

moments.title: Migration utilities
moments.detail: Offered tooling to convert existing GL Wand reports, lowering switching cost.

moments.title: Timeline secured
moments.detail: January execution, June pilot, October Big Bang go-live, plus a P&L template.

moments.title: No agenda or discovery
moments.detail: Went straight to screen share with no recap of requirements or check of attendees' roles.

moments.title: Negative self-framing
moments.detail: Called his own role list 'far too many and far too confusing'.

moments.title: Cost-centre lookup failed
moments.detail: Errored on a direct customer question. 'Something I haven't done before'.

moments.title: Did not know Excel's row limit
moments.detail: '250,000 or a million'. The limit is 1,048,576 rows per sheet.

moments.title: Contradiction on EPM
moments.detail: Marc: a version is coming. Daniel: available now.

moments.title: Bursting failed live
moments.detail: Moved on without showing an output workbook or schedule.

moments.title: AI answer with nothing to show
moments.detail: No date, then a long monologue on attitudes to AI.

moments.title: Unproven differentiation
moments.detail: Enterprise and speed claims with no numbers or references. Competitors not addressed.

moments.title: Second contradiction
moments.detail: Sellers disagreed on whether non-finance data fits in GL Connect.

moments.title: Core driver found late
moments.detail: GL Wand end of support on Fusion and Spreadsheet Server surfaced with 5 minutes left.

moments.title: Pre-brief declined, no date
moments.detail: Request for 30 minutes with a super user was pushed back. No finance demo slot booked.

improvements.happened: Screen share started at 0:00. The buying driver appeared at 41:45.
improvements.instead: Spend the first 8 to 10 minutes confirming roles, the driver (GL Wand on Fusion), competitors in play (GLSense, Spreadsheet Server) and the decision timeline.

improvements.happened: Generic Vision P&L. Priya's requirements list was already in hand.
improvements.instead: Build the demo on a K&S-style P&L and walk their requirements list in order, ticking each off on screen.

improvements.happened: Account plus cost-centre and bursting both failed.
improvements.instead: Dry-run every segment combination and bursting end to end. Keep a recorded backup of each risky flow.

improvements.happened: IT leads attended a finance-user demo.
improvements.instead: For IT, lead with a one-page architecture: ADW schema, security, refresh, latency. Save formula-building depth for the finance session.

improvements.happened: Two contradictions on EPM and non-finance data.
improvements.instead: Agree beforehand who answers product, technical and commercial questions. The second speaker adds, never corrects in front of the buyer.

improvements.happened: Enterprise and speed claims without evidence.
improvements.instead: Show a timed refresh at K&S-like volume, name a comparable reference customer and address Spreadsheet Server and GLSense directly.

improvements.happened: Excel row limit and AI timing were guessed.
improvements.instead: Carry a fact sheet: limits, connector status, release dates. Say 'I will confirm by Friday' instead of guessing.

improvements.happened: No finance demo booked, pre-brief declined.
improvements.instead: Ask for the slot on the call, send a recap within 24 hours with a mutual action plan, and turn the pre-brief into 3 emailed questions.

improvements.happened: About 10 apologies or hedges from the sellers.
improvements.instead: Replace 'excuse me, on the fly' with a confident line such as 'let me show you the cost-centre version in the follow-up'.

actions.action: Investigate cost-centre lookup error and update Priya and Vikash
Confirm finance and P&A availability, propose slots
Email P&L template so the demo can be tailored
30-minute pre-brief with a finance super user
